title: Check, checkmate or neither? (part 1 of 4)
sources: content/lessons/L-FND-CHECK-1.json (the three ways out are taught there, not repeated)
items IBds11-22..35 (shipped; claims checked by tools/validate.py) and content/items/lesson-bg-l-fnd-check-2.json (IBG-LFNDCHECK2-1..13)
Dan Heisman, advice to list the opponent's checks and captures before moving: [S] chess.com article 'passive vs basic hope chess' via docs/citable-views.md 10.4 (paraphrased)
The four-question order is this project's rule of thumb [I]; the guess about practice is [H]
Positions replayed or constructed and checked with python-chess; the short game is a sequence of legal moves (moves are facts)

steps.caption: Black is in check: the white queen looks down a diagonal at the black king. Black has exactly one legal move. Step through it.

line.say: The pawn steps into the queen's line, so the queen no longer reaches the king. Blocking is one way out of check.

steps.text: Every position gets one of three labels. **Check**: the king is attacked, and it has a way out. **Checkmate**: the king is attacked and every way out is closed. **Neither**: the king is not attacked at all. Start with one question only: is the king attacked right now? Trace every line that ends on the king.

steps.caption: Checkmate, questions in order. Attacked? Yes, by the rook along the eighth row. Can anything of Black's take the rook? No. Can anything step in the way? No. Does the king have a safe square? No: three pawns fill the front, and h8 is covered too, as the next board shows.

The king cannot step along the rook's line away from the rook. Once it leaves, the rook's line extends through its old square, so h8 is covered. Moving there is illegal. Learners often miss this and think the king has a flight square.

steps.text: These are the **four questions**, in this order. One: is the king attacked? If not, it is neither, and you stop. Two: can the checker be captured? Three: can something go in the way? Four: does the king have a safe square? Any yes after the first means only check. [I] The order runs from cheapest to dearest: a capture is one look, a block takes a search, king squares come last. It settles almost every position; double check is the exception.

steps.caption: Two pieces giving check at once is a double check. Taking or blocking cannot answer both, so only a king move works. [I] Questions two and three are skipped here. The double-check lesson goes deeper.
Question one gets a no. The white rook looks up the h-file, but Black's own pawn stands in the way, so the king is not attacked. Neither. Stop there; the other questions are not needed.
